raw_response:
I am 64 years old, finished junior high, and I have farmed these fields in Quzhou for 38 years. My household is just me and my wife, and we have 10.1 mu total — 7 mu I keep in wheat-maize rotation, and 3.1 mu I grow cotton because the price was alright last year and I have the well to water it. For the wheat already in the ground, I sowed Jimai 22 last fall at 22 jin per mu and put down one 50-jin bag of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer per mu as base. This spring I will top-dress with 30 jin of urea per mu at green-up, and another 10 jin at jointing if the wheat looks strong, which comes to about 16 kg of pure nitrogen per mu for the season, plus 7 kg each of phosphorus and potassium from the base. I will irrigate three times from the well — green-up, jointing, and grain-filling — and spray twice, once for weeds and once for insects at heading. Last year I got 500 kg per mu and I expect the same this year if the weather holds. For the summer maize after wheat harvest, I will plant Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed at 3 jin per mu and hire a no-tillage seeder for 40 yuan per mu to save time. I will put 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at planting and top-dress with 20 jin of urea at big trumpet stage, so that is 15 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 6 kg potassium per mu. I will irrigate twice and spray twice for weeds and armyworm, and I expect 600 kg per mu. For cotton on the 3.1 mu, I will rotary-till in April, lay plastic mulch, and plant hybrid cotton seed. I will use one bag of compound fertilizer per mu as base and top-dress with 15 jin of urea total, giving 14 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 6 kg potassium per mu. Cotton needs three irrigations and four sprays for bollworm and aphids, which is a lot of work, but I can still manage it with just the two of us. I expect 240 kg of seed cotton per mu. Fertilizer is expensive now — urea is over 100 yuan per 50-jin bag — but I learned long ago that I would rather waste half a bag than lose yield. A bad harvest is a disaster; wasting fertilizer is just a cost. I also have to think about my whole budget: if I spend too much on fertilizer, I have less for hiring labor or extra pesticide. So I mostly do what I did last year and I watch what Lao Wang and Lao Li do. If they use about the same amounts and their fields look good, then I feel safe. I don't try new things unless I see them work in someone else's field first.
